Two Laredo marching bands are headed to the state stage. J.B. Alexander High School and United High School both earned spots at the UIL 6A State Marching Band Contest after strong finishes at the UIL Area G contest, according to United Independent School District.

Among 16 competing bands, Alexander and United finished first and second, respectively, in the preliminary round and advanced to the finals. Alexander went on to claim first place and the UIL Area G Championship, while United secured third place, earning the district two of the three available qualifying spots for state.

The win marks Alexander's fifth UIL Area G Championship and its eighth consecutive trip to the State Marching Contest. Head Band Director Ricardo Fuentes leads a 325-student program, and he said the achievement is about more than trophies — the character, relationships and lives changed through the experience will endure long after the final performance.

For United, the finish marks a return to the state stage for the first time since 2023 and the program's fifth trip in school history. Head Band Director Samuel Hjort credited the students' dedication and the foundation built by the program's former leadership, middle school music educators and supportive families.

UISD Superintendent Dr. Gerardo Cruz called the achievement a testament to the dedication of the student musicians, band directors, support staff and families, whose months of early morning practices and long rehearsals led to this moment.

The UIL 6A State Marching Band Contest takes place Monday, November 9, at the Alamodome in San Antonio. The United Longhorn Band is scheduled to perform at 11:45 a.m., and the Alexander Bulldog Band takes the field at 9:00 p.m.

Before they leave, the community can wish both bands well at send-offs today, Sunday, November 8. United's lineup begins at 11:30 a.m. along International Boulevard near United High School. Alexander lines up at 3:30 p.m. at the SAC along Santa Claudia Lane. The district invites families, alumni and the entire community to bring signs, wear school colors and make some noise.

Alexander and United have advanced to the State Marching Contest together only twice before, in 2018 and 2023. Their third shared appearance is another proud moment for both schools and for Laredo, UISD Fine Arts Director Joshua Martinez said, urging the community to show up with pride and give both bands the support they have earned.

Source: United Independent School District, November 5, 2026.

title: Alexander and United bands march to UIL State — send-offs today, contest Monday in San Antonio
